correctness.rationale: For U before V the three full prefix-width formulas are (a+b), (t-a+b+1), and (2t-a-b). A hub exchange in width t necessarily exposes a center cut of width at least t+1. Five local normalization classes have explicitly checked cut changes, giving a feasible O(t^2) route to the common canonical ordering within either hub orientation for every k>=t. The class word A^h B^h U V A^(t-h) B^(t-h), h=floor(t/2), has width t+1 in both hub orders, producing an actual interorientation swap. Recurrence F_t counts exactly the t-budget symbolic prefixes with the stated widths, multiplied by (t!)^2 assignments of labels. Direct-edge enumeration independently confirms full feasible graphs, connectivity, counts and canonical paths for t=1,2,3 (up to 13536 states), with deterministic random testing through t=14. These checks do not replace the all-t proof.

value.rationale: The motivating general factor-two resource guarantee leaves open the minimal extra capacity for actual reachability in sparse network layouts. Here the obstruction caused by two adjacent high-degree hubs is exactly identified: at the tight threshold there are two huge orientation components with exact finite-state counts, while precisely one additional crossing edge of capacity permits an explicit transition, for every branching parameter t. The constructive O(t^2) route makes the threshold algorithmically meaningful and extends structural understanding beyond the related single-hub case.
